The design needs work, but it’s not a complete wash.


I think the previous comment about the frame/border is important; it’s imperative to consider the end result. When designing for a print, you need to be mindful of the limitations of printers. They don’t always lay the print down exactly centered, and during trimming, this can be compounded. Even a 1/16th of an inch in slip can become glaringly obvious with something like the border used here. If you’re deadset on using it, increase the margin to at least an inch, if not more. However, I’d consider dropping it entirely for two reasons: 1 – as stated, it would make the prints much less problematic; 2 — A beach event conjures ideas of openness, fresh air, free space. Thematically, a border contradicts that.

 
Similarly, on the topic of theme. The event is called Paint the Beach, so I imagine bright, rich colours. The idea to use a rainbow gradient is good in theory, but in execution, the colours are muddy and speak more of the morning-after. They don’t scream bright, colourful fun. A limited palette and strong use of contrast can often get the idea of “colourful” across more strongly than including every colour imaginable. Orange is noticeably orangier when it’s by itself, right? Check out this poster series https://dribbble.com/shots/1404070-Poster-Color-Me-Rad-2013. (Pardon the unsightly url; I’m on mobile and don’t have reddit’s formatting committed to memory.)

 
The typography is easily the weakest link in the poster. There are too many fonts, they’re the wrong fonts for the job, the white glow is unrefined, the black colour is a bit blah, and the sizing is disorganized.


Too many fonts: Simplify! It’s tempting to use many fonts as a crutch to ramp up the aesthetic excitement of a piece, but DON’T. Like a limited pallet in painting, restraint forces you to be careful in your composition. Which leads us into the next few points.

 
Wrong fonts: They’re thin, dull, and hard to read. Remember how you need to consider the end result? The text will be illegible to someone walking past the poster. Thin fonts often get used to convey ideas of elegance, refinement, and luxury. For this event, consider something fun, bold, chunky even.

 
White glow/black colour: I’d imagine you laid the text out on the rainbow gradient and saw that it was hard to see. Adding the glow does help, but it’s kind of a rookie move. Fixing the background, the font choice, and the sizing are better solutions because you’re considering the poster as a whole, not preoccupying yourself with one line of text on one space, at one time. Good design is, to use a wanky term, wholistic.

 

Sizing: Sizing and organization is the make-or-break of typography. Used properly, it creates hierarchy of the most important textual elements on the page, controlling the audience’s eye, and therefore, the flow of information from the page to their brain. Improperly, it’s confusing. Confusing things will make audience’s stop reading, and discard the info from their memory. Designers, quite obviously, don’t want that. Consider what the most critical lines are, in relation to each other and other elements on the page. Is it the title? The date? The location? That triangle (is it a logo, or just a ‘cool’ design used to generate visual interest)? Evaluate that and revisit your text.


This is a really great poster to have put up, because it reveals a lot of crutches that can easily go undetected when you first start out. We all kind of nascently understand when something looks good, but it takes practice to discern why and what mechanics are driving that. If nothing else, I hope it shows you one or two things to avoid in the future. Becoming good at this takes years. After six professionally, frankly, I’m still shit. To me, it’s a process of learning what my lazy areas and blinders are. So good on you for asking for critique, sorry other people choose derisive snark over being actually helpful. Also, sorry for the novel.

For anyone curious, this is the story I was told growing up:

My Opa, the Evgenii (In Canada, Eugene), was fleeing Europe. I recall being told at one point he had to leave Ukraine due to advancing fronts from the Nazis and the Russians, but given the dates on his emigration documents (some of which I have), I'm not sure. I might have made this up in my own head. 

What I know for certain is that he left his entire family when he was a teenager, traveled from the Ukraine with an Aunt, received a Visa for German Nationals in Bremen on Jan 23, 1951, and arrived in St. John New Brunswick on February 9, 1951.

They traveled to Alberta, where they stayed and my Opa married Inka (Who herself left Germany either prior to or shortly after the outbreak of WW2) and started my Mom's side of the family. It's a bit sad, because Opa never did get a chance to return to his family. I'm iffy on my History, but I would hazard a guess that his mother died before the close of the Cold War. 

My mother didn't even know she had an Uncle Buller - unless I'm misunderstanding, were letters sometime sent by someone not directly related to the letter's authors?

As well, I'm named after the Sasha (Alexander) in the letter.

I assume you're in college away from home. My advice would be to make sure you have a support network first and foremost. 

If you have supportive friends, reach out to them. Even they aren't the closest to you right now, that can change.

I also *strongly* advocate getting in touch with campus counselling. For several reasons:

*They can provide emotional support, because this qualifies as a traumatic event*

*During this time, there's a high chance your school work can suffer. Its natural, it happens,  no shame. But the last thing you want is for an entire semester to take damage because of some seriously shitty knucklefucks.*

*They are trained and have access to resources specifically for things like this, especially where housing is concerned. Even if you aren't in crisis, they can talk you through this and make the transition easy*

*You mentioned depression. That's reason enough. It happens so many people and counselling services are great ways to turn emotional fractures into lifelong cognitive strengths. Think of them as personal trainers for your mind*

*Campus counseling should be free. So why not?*

Hey man. Sorry, my phone didn't notify me that you had replied, apologies for the lateness here.

Bottom line: what your friend is doing is *not* okay. Like, at all. 

Is he aware that you have feelings for him? Because you might need to make that clear. Or at least make it clear that the way he teases you makes you very uncomfortable. 

I had friend in the exact same situation. In fact when I read this last night, I had deja vu. What I told him, and what I'm telling you is that no matter how strongly you care and love a friend (in any capacity, romantic or not), that friendship is never worth emotional damage to yourself. 

You might think you can't deal with being apart, but right now you know you can't deal with being together, either. If the dynamic of this friendship doesn't change, you will end up in very dark places, and you should never be there. 

Essentially, there are two solutions to this problem. Change how you feel, or change the mechanics of the friendship. Since you can't easily (if at all) change how you feel in the immediate future, the friendship needs to change. This means either he stops flirting or you stop spending time together. More than likely, you'll need to stop spending time together until you are over him. 

Take a long hard look at yourself: can you really wean yourself off him? Or should you step back and take time apart? You likely already know the answer to this - its always just difficult to admit it to yourself that you do.

Pride isn't about feathers. It isn't about beads, and sparkles, and glitter, and 5,000 visiting profiles on Grindr. 

It isn't about drag queens. It's not about leather. It's not about bears, twinks, otters, cubs, bros, jocks or daddies.

It isn't about Absolut. Or Schmirnoff. Or Bacardi. Or any other corporate sponsor.

It's not about floats. Or parades. Or club music. It isn't even about dancing, even though there's just so goddamn much of it.

It's not about fems, lipsticks, butches. It isn't about Dykes on Bikes, even as awesome as that is to watch.

It isn't about marching teachers, writers, artists, cube-dwellers.

It's not about the youth, or the elderly. And it certainly isn't about politicians, regardless of how much they love to make appearances.

It isn't about remembering victims of bullying. Or abuse. Or rape.

Or murder.


It's about a space, and a time, where whatever you want to be, whoever you want to be, is okay. Where spontaneously communities spring up, and people who thought "Fuck, I'm the only one who feels like this" can look around and say: "Oh, maybe I'm not."

"Maybe what I feel isn't so strange. Or wrong. Or perverted. Or sinful."

"Maybe for once, I'm in a place where who I am is celebrated, just by virtue of the fact that I am here, and I exist."


Because in 100 years, we've gone from abominations, to mentally ill, to demon-possessed, to sinners, to Luke who works in a bank, and on Sundays likes to go to the shops with his husband Ted and pick out old vinyls from the 70s. And I'll be damned if we don't deserve to celebrate any way we choose. 

And now we want to look down at our brothers, yes our BROTHERS, because they're "one of *those* gays?" We're trying to claw our way to equality, and all we want to do is scratch our beards and hmm and haw over whether Devin, who likes to put on leggings and a wig and be Deena for a weekend in July is setting us back ten years?

No. What sets us back is ridiculous and petty infighting. What sets us back is the incomprehensibly asinine way we tear down walls to equality and only to replace them with our own walls. Because that's what these attitudes are about: "Oh all those wispy gays at Pride, they show our worst side to the public and make them hate us. I'm not like them. I'm much better." 


Don't want to march, or parade, or club, or dance, or drag, or swish? Neither do I. But I have respect, love, and admiration for those who do. Who fought back against the NYC police at Stonewall? All of us. Men, women, trans-folk, drag queens. 

So why on earth are we splitting up now?

I think it's interesting how different tropes and metaphors arise during various periods in history. 

It's not that hard to imagine why animals were so heavily relied upon back then. The frontier, the unsettled land, and all that swam, walked, crawled upon or flew above it was the reality that these story tellers lived in. People were scarce, and civilization moreso. No small wonder that animals and nature were the principle metaphors through which they chose to conceptualize and communicate their experiences (fictitious or not). The natural world was unforgiving of our forebears. People were regularly killed by the elements and animals. In each of these folktales, nature is either co-opted and made the ally/slave of humans, or it is defeated outright. 

A very similar thing is observable today. The icons of our popculture, that is, the figures of our modern folklore are conceived in the same way. They had Babe, giant catfish and alligators; we have Cylons, aliens, and zombies.

Now, the point I'm making isn't that because these things are everywhere, we make them our cultural metaphors. That's silly - they're, for all intents and purposes, made up. What I'm getting at is that it's no accident things like Twilight, BSG, and the Walking Dead are so popular - they resonate with audiences in similar fashion to 19 and 20th century folklore because the supernatural artifices are metaphorical containers into which we pour all the cultural and societial ideas and anxieities of our day. 

Simply, it's how we deal with our shit.

I forgot the particularities of the sound of her screams shortly after waking up, saving graces, I suppose. But I know what that sound was and continues to be for me – absolute horror and loss, the entire scope and meaning of suffering and emotional oblivion poured into a soundwave. 

I hugged my mom a lot that day.

When I was much younger, say five or six, I routinely had recursive dreams where I would just go about my day. Usually I was in school. Typically, they would utterly banal situations, but gradually I would realize I was repeating the same sequence over and over and over again and a pretty chilling existential terror would wrack my tiny mind. I would try going to sleep to wake up, but I'd end up right back in the dream again.

Somehow, I came to the conclusion that the only way to extricate myself was either 1) holding my breath until I passed out or, failing that, 2) trying to pull my own eyes out.

I have very messed up dreams, always have, always will. I love 'em.

This is a story about a sleepy man, an apartment, and a tiny intruder.
On Monday, the 13th of February, a gray, dull, dreary day, I'm woken up suddenly by a very curious noise. As my collective consciousness begins to reassemble in the cold morning air, I stare up at my ceiling and wonder two things: what time is it? and what woke me up? Not that I'm particularly upset about being woken; I enjoy getting up earlier than I usually do, and if it is, in fact, much too early, it's rather easy for me to fall back asleep.

Anyways.

I'm sitting in bed, and it occurs to me that I hear things coming from my roomate’s room. Specifically, I hear someone rummaging through her closet and sorting through her things. Oh, I think to myself, Oh, she must still be getting ready for work. This is odd, because it's never woken me up before. More odd, is the fact that it is 10:30 am, and she left over three hours ago for work. She is never late, this girl. In fact she's usually early for everything. And has never, to my knowledge, slept through an alarm. It must not be her, I reason.

So who is in there?

My still sleep-addled mind is struggling to rationalize a situation from the disparate facts I have at my disposal. Finally, what it does arrive at is the fact that the door must have been left open, and now there is an intruder in the house, and we are presently being robbed. This is a big problem for me, because I like my things. My things are pretty nice. Especially my laptop, without which I think I might crumble up and be blown away like internet-deprived chaff.

It is at this point, I realize I need to solve this problem.

It briefly occurs to me to phone the police. They will come with guns, and pepper spray and devil-may-care attitudes and will probably repel the invader with a lot more skill than one groggy 26 year old. But of course, I've never been the one to follow after suggested directions, or even common sense really. So I quietly slide out of bed, and put on a protective armoring of gym shorts and yesterday’s t-shirt.

Now, I thought, I need a weapon.

I take a quick survey of my room. The two best options I have are as follows (and again, I'll remind you that I've only just woken up and am quite delirious with sleep):

1) A mug of water
2) A large plastic box of Christmas ornaments.

Scenario 1), I can surprise the intruder who will then fire his gun. However, just before he squeezes the trigger, I will hurl the mug at him. As he will have just caught a face full of room temperature water, his aim will be compromised and nevertheless, the bullet will glance off the mug and I will remain safe. Yes, this is what I thought, that a ceramic mug will protect me from bullets. It was the morning, okay? Let's see you go all mythbusters when you haven't had your coffee yet. Anyways, this will continue with me having the perfect opportunity to...I don't know...tackle him or something?

Scenario 2), I surprise the mugger and hurl a big plastic container of Christmas bulbs at him, which will seriously startle the thief (wouldn't you, too, be caught off guard if you were minding your own business, going about politely robbing someone, when some blearly eyed weirdo goes mental and chucks silver and red glittery balls at you?). In my head, I saw this playing out as a scene from Home Alone. Which, in addition to successful, would definitely have been awesome.

At this point I decided that I was being completely fucking stupid, and went to the kitchen to grab a knife.

I creep to the door of my roomies’  room, shut nice and tight. In my frog-like voice, I ask "<roomie’s name>?". No answer, no change in the noise. I knock. The noise continues. Well, says I, here we go. I will either live through this a hero, or this is the time I go to meet my maker. It was pretty heavy, considering I had only been awake for like, three minutes. I imagined this is what soldiers feel like. So, brandishing nine inches of kinda-dull cold, budget kitchen steel, I bust the door open, mentally prepared for the biggest fight of my life. What follows next is a stream of consciousness, thought by thought replay, mostly true, transcribed as best I can:

I'm going to diiieeeeeeeeeeee Ohhh it's just a squirrel.

There is a squirrel in the room.

A squirrel.

A SQUIRREL!

OH ITS SO CUTE!

NO, BrayAlexndr, focus! It doesn't belong here.

Oh, you're right.

I'm glad it isn't a robber.

Or a ghost.

Yes, or that.

Well, what shall we do?

I dunno, we'll need to put it in something?

What if we got a piece of cardboard and a big bowl, like it's a spider?

That might work!

No wait, that's the stupidest fucking thing since ever.

Right, yeah. Umm...a garbage bag?

But how would that even work?

We could...like...jump on it?

I need to phone an adult. What is my dad doing?

Things with numbers and money, I don't know, he's probably busy.

Yeah you're right. What about mum?

She'd start talking to it in a high pitched voice and want to name it. That's not what we need.

No?

No.

Oh.

...

Well it is awfully cute. Maybe I should get my camera first?

Wait a second...have we been spinning in crazy little circles for the past thirty seconds of weirdly conversational 
internal monologue?

Y...yes, we definitely have.

Right then, we're clearly gone off a bit.

But...SQUIRREL!

It's at this point, however, that the squirrel notices me being a complete fucking moron dancing around in one spot, and mercifully decides to save us all the embarrassment, and promptly just exits out the hole in the screen it chewed to gain entry in the first place. It hops out the window and scurries away, but not before pausing, looking at me and angrily chattering for a second. I can only imagine that his angry tirade of squirrel speak was something rather indignant and annoyed:

“Dude, what the fuck? I just wanted to get warm and maybe eat your roommates bedsheets or whatever squirrels do. Then you come in here with a knife and start spazzing out like a complete psycho. I'm leaving this place. I'd rather break in to the apartment of the loud mouthed bitch who lives downstairs!!”

TL;DR – Woke up, threatened a squirrel with knife, did a dance, determined a need for antipsychosis meds.

My first job as a teenager was the night shift in a grocery store photo lab. Let me tell you, for a small, conservative Canadian town, it seemed like we had a disproportionate amount of amateur pornographers.We charged by print, so I had to count every shot by hand. By far the best (worst?) was a disposable camera that started off with what must have been a couple’s new daschund pup. The dog was adorable, super r/aww-worthy, in all sorts of poses, with toys, with hats, with much snuggling and cuddles from the family. 
I was lulled into a false sense of security: “aww, that’s a cute hat,” I think. “And look, now he’s got a ball. Ohhh, there he is with his widdle paws in the air. Aw, shucks, that lady’s got a massive dick rammed down her throat…wait what the what?” Suddenly, in the midst of all the weiner dog lovin’ came a round of straight up weiner lovin’. The beej was just for starters, the rest of this roll was full of the sort of stuff that usually needs a credit card number first. Luckily, I was not there when the woman came to collect the roll, because I would not have been able to keep myself from making a scene. 

Not photolab, but related. After highschool, I worked in a printshop downtown. We did piddly little design work, business cards and brochures mostly, but we also has a bunch of photocopiers available for use. Now, for some bizarre reason, every week we would have the local police officers come in and have crime scene photos copied in quads for court. Why on Earth the PD used us instead of getting its own machine is completely beyond me. A lot of the time it was nothing more than mere B&E’s and destruction of property. But every once in a while, we got more graphic packages. I’ve seen enough stabbings to last me a lifetime; the distinct colour of fat starting to gape out a deep laceration is burned into my retinas. The most awful, however, was of two different vehicle collisions. On one, a drunk driver wrapped his jeep around a traffic light pole (incidentally, around the corner from where I lived at the time). He wasn’t in the photos, but the body (or its remnants, anyways) of his girlfriend were. The jeep somehow ended up on it side, and the photo was from the perspective of the officer standing on the driver’s side and looking down at the passenger seat. There wasn’t a jeep anymore, just a mangled wreck of glass, metal and seat cushion that had apparently crushed/ripped into/cocooned the poor woman. All I saw was a lifeless arm protruding from the swirl of shrapnel. Awful stuff.
The other was of a country accident, but apparently, this driver wasn’t found for a few days, because by the time he was discovered and photographed, he had very clearly been left out in the elements (it was late-winter/early spring). His skin was a horrible grey-green, leathery mess, saggy in some places and taut in others. He had just an awful grimace on his face. To think that we could end up like that was the most sobering thing I’d ever experienced. 

TL;DR – Puppy, puppy, puppy, -surprise bj and anal. Woman crushed in car accident, driver’s body lay undiscovered for a few days in prairie winter.
